pages.text: Tap, tap, tap! A woodpecker's sound came through the loft window. Nils the little bear pulled the covers over his head. "Mmm... Woodpecker, tap a little later."
From below the loft, Grandpa Bruno of the forest cabin called, "Bread is baked. Eat, then let's go to the garden." "I want warm bread! But just a little longer..." Nils didn't move and slept again.
When he climbed down, sunlight reached the middle of the loft. Table bread was already cold and hard. Grandpa had been to the garden. "Oh? Already?" Nils pouted.
Grandpa sat on the floor beside him. "A waking body is folded up. Stretch it long like this." His broad palm supported Nils's paw as they reached up together.

Front paws stretch, back paws stretch! As his body grew long, Nils's closed eyes opened wide. "Stretching chased sleep away!" His eyes sparkled, awake. Grandpa smiled. "Tomorrow morning, like this. Tap, tap, tap—jump up!"
The next morning, tap, tap, tap! The woodpecker tapped a tree. Nils kicked off the covers and jumped up! Front paws up, back paws stretch! "Tap, tap, tap—jump up!" Sleep flew away.
Nils pushed the loft window with both paws. Creak! Half open. He peeped his face through, smelling wet soil. Standing on his toes, he called, "Hello, morning! Tap, tap, tap—jump up!"
By the well's water tub, Nils scooped cold water in both paws and pressed it to his cheeks. His shoulders lifted by themselves. Wet fur lay smooth. "I started the morning myself!"
Three morning steps. "One, tap, tap, tap—jump up! Two, window open, say hello! Three, wash at the tub!" Steam rose from the bread. Nils raised both paws above his head. "Warm and fresh!"
Grandpa hugged him tight. "Up before the bread today!" Jump up at the tapping, and you miss none of the morning. "Tap, tap, tap—jump up! Grandpa, let's go to the garden!"
